pos.personaBrief: Klopp 2013: 'I don't like winning with 80 per cent'; Rangnick: 'just having the ball ourselves doesn't make sense'; Liverpool still had ~60% but Red Bull wins the ball high and attacks fast, so possession is a means, not a goal.

pro.personaBrief: Rangnick hates square and back passes and wants few touches after a regain; Leipzig laser passes, Salzburg long balls, StatsBomb says best chances come from quick transitions.

est.personaBrief: Players swarm the ball zone in pressing and rotate (Nagelsmann rotations, versatile players, Liverpool's Firmino dropping, fluid full-backs), though pressing patterns are rehearsed.

lar.personaBrief: Liverpool attack through high full-backs with inverted narrow forwards; Leipzig used 4-2-2-2 or a diamond with central rotations; vertical play through the middle and wide when the block is packed.

blo.personaBrief: Core of the ideology: high press, counter-pressing immediately after losing the ball, forwards pressing from the first pass, traps; regains high up the pitch are the main chance creator.

mar.personaBrief: Mixed evidence: Red Bull open-play press is man-oriented (Salzburg, Rangnick back line marking strikers), Leipzig set pieces mix five zonal markers with man-markers, Liverpool's marking unverified.

pla.personaBrief: A fixed, imposed model: press high and attack vertically whoever the opponent (Klopp's 'fighting football', Rangnick's rehearsed pressing, Marsch's contagious overwhelming); Nagelsmann adapts more but the school imposes its idea.

res.personaBrief: Heavy metal, loud, fighting, spectacle-oriented football that goes for the win; no sitting back for a draw away or to protect a lead; style matters over mere result.

sis.personaBrief: System-driven: Rangnick recruits players suited to his way, everyone presses, Alisson says nobody is special at Liverpool, Leipzig and Salzburg make ordinary young players perform through the pressing system.

jog.personaBrief: Physical output is the base: Marsch says it requires big physical output, Rangnick wants strong, quick under-23s, Liverpool's midfield valued work ethic and discipline over talent; a classic non-running 10 has no place.

bas.personaBrief: Red Bull buys young prospects (Leipzig signings average 21, Salzburg kicks players out at 22, Rangnick wants under-23s) and sells them; Klopp used experienced stars; squads are built by signing, not academy loyalty.

lid.personaBrief: Equal rules for all (Alisson: nobody is special), Nagelsmann says 70% social competence, Klopp can shut up arguing players, Rangnick/Klopp are firm bosses but caring and loud.
